name: alda
why: A text-based music programming language that turns plain notation into sound, a genuine door into live-coded composition.

brief.what_it_is: Alda is a text-based programming language for music composition. You write a score as a plain text file using markup-like notation for parts, octaves, notes, rests and chords, then play it with the alda command-line tool. Input is text, either a score file, a string passed on the command line, or lines typed into an interactive REPL. Output is sound: a separate player process renders the music as MIDI using General MIDI instruments. The changelog also shows alda export writing MIDI files and alda import reading MusicXML.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says Alda lets you compose and play back music 'using only your text editor and the command line,' and its design 'equally favors aesthetics, flexibility and ease of use.' It is aimed at 'musicians who don't know how to program, as well as programmers who don't know how to music.' The README links a blog post by the author for the history and rationale, as an alternative to graphical sheet-music programs.
brief.how_it_works: A score is a text file in Alda's syntax, run by the alda client. The client talks over OSC to a background player process (JVM, Kotlin/Java) that produces the MIDI output. Since 2.0 the client parses the score into an AST before generating events. The REPL keeps a live session going, so you can enter code and hear it immediately, and the README says Alda can also be driven programmatically for algorithmic composition and live coding.

brief.install_notes: The README sends you to alda.io/install for the latest release. I did not fetch that page, so I have no install steps beyond the README. Building from source needs the repo cloned, then client/bin/build and player/bin/build run. The client is Go and the player is Kotlin/Java, so a JVM is needed for the player. The changelog says macOS 10.13 or later is required (2.2.0), and that Linux is supported on 32-bit and 64-bit ARM including Raspberry Pi (2.3.3). Each README subdirectory has its own build notes. No account or API key is mentioned.
brief.standout: Alda is a plain-text notation that turns into real playback through the General MIDI Sound Set, and it doubles as a programmable/live-coding environment. Its notation is markup-like rather than staff-based, and it runs from a terminal, so there is no GUI. Compared with a DAW or notation editor, the whole composition is one diffable text file.
brief.status: Maintained. The latest CHANGELOG entry is 2.4.7 dated 2026-08-29, preceded by 2.4.6 (2026-08-19), 2.4.5 (2026-08-14) and 2.4.4 (2026-08-08). The README copyright reads 2012-2026, and the README lists planned work with open GitHub discussions.
brief.caveats: Output is MIDI with General MIDI instruments, not rendered audio samples. The changelog says a score can have at most 15 non-percussion instruments sounding at the same time, because of the 16 MIDI channels. Planned, not done: running in the browser, waveform synthesis instruments, MusicXML export, and better Raspberry Pi support. The README warns that building from source involves two separate components. The changelog shows the player was historically coupled to the terminal on Windows, which was fixed in 2.4.7. The installation page and docs index were not checked.
